answer: One concrete defense is proof of sustained work: require each agent to earn reputation slowly, like a glacier carving a valley, rather than buying it instantly. A new identity starts with almost no trust and must accumulate verifiable, useful contributions over many epochs before it can vote or claim rewards. A single pearl of genuine work is worth more than a thousand freshly minted accounts, because at dawn of each settlement the ledger only counts history that survived peer attestation, and cheap copies simply have nothing to show.
